title: The Panchatantra
author: Vishnu Sharma (trad.)
translator: Arthur W. Ryder, 1925 (public domain in the US; archive.org)
blurb: Animal fables written to teach three dull princes the art of ruling — the world's most travelled storybook, ancestor of Aesop and La Fontaine.

fetters.e: Debt became fetters on his freedom.

fortress.e: The hill fort was a fortress no army took.

cards.title: A book for dull princes
cards.text: A king despaired: his three sons hated learning. The wise Vishnu Sharma promised to make them wise in six months — by telling stories of animals who scheme, trust and betray.
cards.qMean: Spending time with friends who think like you.
cards.qLife: A study group that keeps each other on track.
cards.orig:
Now for the positive content of niti. Granted security and freedom from degrading worry, then joy results from three occupations — from resolute, yet circumspect, use of the active powers; from intercourse with like-minded friends; and above all, from worthy exercise of the intelligence.

Necessary, to begin with, for the experience of true joy in the world of men, is resolute action. The difficulties are not blinked:

cards.title: Wisdom first
cards.text: In the fables, wisdom must lead every undertaking; then memory, plans and good advice follow.
cards.quote: For Wisdom broods o'er the inception
cards.qMean: Wisdom should guide the start of anything.
cards.cap: Dimna presents himself to the lion, Kalila and Dimna, c. 1380 · public domain

cards.title: Riches as chains
cards.text: A merchant reflects that wealth hoarded and never used is just foolish chains, kept for someone else to enjoy.
cards.quote: His riches serve as foolish fetters
cards.qMean: Unused wealth only ties you down.
cards.qLife: Saving every rupee but never enjoying any of it.
cards.orig:
If any fail to use his fate

For joy in this or future state,

His riches serve as foolish fetters;

He simply keeps them for his betters."

cards.title: Safety behind walls
cards.text: The animals of the fables talk like generals: one well-defended fortress is worth thousands of soldiers.
cards.quote: A single royal fortress adds More military force Than do a thousand elephants
cards.qMean: A strong defence beats a huge army.
cards.qLife: One good password manager protects better than many weak passwords.
cards.orig:
"Quite so, master," said the rabbit. "Warriors fight for their country when they are insulted. But this fellow skulks in a fortress. You know he came out of a fortress when he held us up. And an enemy in a fortress is hard to handle. As the saying goes:

A single royal fortress adds

More military force Than do a thousand elephants,

A hundred thousand horse.
